item.title: C$470 million payout for Nova Scotia workers after court strikes down wage restriction law
item.description: Public sector workers in Canada's Nova Scotia province could receive up to C$5,000 each under a C$470 million compensation deal approved by a court. The settlement follows a ruling that declared a 2015 law restricting wage increases and long-service benefits unconstitutional. Around 81,000 workers may qualify for wage-related damages, while payments must be completed by December 31, 2027.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sydney buyers win court fight over promised ocean views
item.description: In a landmark ruling, a New South Wales court has declared a $6.2 million home sale in Bronte void, citing undisclosed development plans. Buyers discovered a looming nine-storey structure that would block their ocean views just after signing the contract. The ruling emphasized that agents misrepresented crucial information. Following the legal wrangling, the property eventually sold for just $5.1 million, underscoring the critical need for transparency in real estate dealings.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Hawaii woman's kindness reunites Chicago family with long-lost photo albums
item.description: Rosa Lopez discovered old family photo albums outside her condominium in Waikiki, Hawaii, and decided to help. After researching, she found the albums belonged to a family in Chicago. Anna Richardson and her mother traveled across the country to retrieve their family memories. Upon meeting Lopez, they reflected on the history preserved in the photographs. This encounter highlights the importance of family history and acts of kindness.
item.dc:creator: World Desk

item.title: Melbourne's 1920 garage-turned-cinema hits market at $2.75 million
item.description: A historic building at 802 High Street, Thornbury, is set to hit the market soon. Initially a motor garage, the property has served various purposes over the years, including an independent cinema. Its renovation in 2018 transformed it into a popular destination combining film screenings with social gatherings. The auction scheduled for December 3 includes the cinema and a residential unit above.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Around six drones swarmed US airbase in Britain, none recovered: Report
item.description: Several unidentified drones reportedly encroached upon RAF Lakenheath, a major US military airbase in Britain. Security alerts prompted US personnel to shelter in place during this incident on November 13. The drones were ultimately repelled using counter-drone technology, although none were recovered. Iranian involvement is suspected, with no confirmation on whether they carried any payload. Security at military installations remains a top priority for both US and UK authorities.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: The NFL team named after Edgar Allan Poe's famous poem has announced a $50,000 gift to help protect the writer's historic Baltimore home from nearby demolition work, as a $3 million museum expansion is planned
item.description: Edgar Allan Poe's historic house in Baltimore faces preservation challenges due to nearby demolition and redevelopment activities. The Baltimore Ravens donated $50,000 to Poe Baltimore to support preservation efforts for the museum. Poe Baltimore has initiated a $3 million campaign to restore the house and expand museum facilities. Plans include creating new exhibition spaces and educational activities centered on Poe's life and contributions.
item.dc:creator: World Desk

item.title: Florida man uses AI to clone streamer’s voice in $260,000 crypto scam; gets 47 months in prison
item.description: In a daring scheme, David Anthony Sanchez pretended to be the well-known streamer N3ON to swindle cryptocurrency enthusiasts, pocketing around $260,000. By leveraging fake profiles, deceptive contracts, and AI-generated voice technology, he crafted an illusion of credibility. His 47-month prison sentence follows his guilty plea, and while he faces restitution to his victims, the specifics remain under wraps. This incident underscores the growing threat of AI-driven scams.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: At 11, he vowed to repay a neighbour’s kindness; now his group has fed 29,000 families at Thanksgiving
item.description: Rob Adams fulfilled a childhood vow to assist needy families by establishing Thanksgiving Heroes. This initiative has grown nationwide, impacting over 29,000 families since it started. The organization prioritizes delivering meals to families selected by their communities, eliminating the need for proof of need. Local affiliates operate independently while maintaining the mission of families assisting families. There are plans to expand meal distributions to 3,600 families by 2026.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: OpenAI vs Apple: ChatGPT maker countersues iPhone maker for stealing trade secrets
item.description: OpenAI has countersued Apple, alleging that the tech giant stole trade secrets and restricted supplier access. This legal conflict stems from claims of employee poaching by Apple, which OpenAI vehemently denies. Apple initially filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and former employees regarding misappropriation of trade secrets. The legal battle coincides with growing competition over artificial intelligence products and proprietary technology.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: She invited a stranger to Thanksgiving in 2016; now their friendship is becoming a movie
item.description: Arizona grandmother Wanda Dench and Jamal Hinton, whose friendship began after she accidentally sent him a Thanksgiving invitation in 2016, are celebrating 10 years of their unusual bond. The duo, who have continued their Thanksgiving tradition through personal losses and major life changes, are now working with Lifetime on a movie based on their story.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Los Angeles mansion sells for $38.65 million after $26.35 million price cut
item.description: In an impressive turn of events, a luxurious mansion known as Villa Serenique in Brentwood has changed hands for $38.65 million, a significant drop from its original asking price of $65 million. Spanning around 20,000 square feet, this exquisite property boasts nine bedrooms and fifteen bathrooms over three levels, catering to every entertainment and relaxation need.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Two American Airlines planes clip wings while taxiing at Washington airport
item.description: Two American Airlines planes clipped their wings while taxiing at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. The incident occurred around 5.10pm ET and led to an emergency response. No injuries were reported as the Federal Aviation Administration began investigating the event. Both aircraft returned to their gates for inspection, after which American Airlines arranged alternative travel for passengers.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: US pushed Venezuela, Iraq to quit OPEC to boost oil output: Report
item.description: The United States influenced both Venezuela and Iraq regarding their membership in OPEC earlier this year. After the removal of Nicolás Maduro, discussions were opened about Venezuela potentially leaving the organization. Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi also contemplated Iraq's OPEC exit amid US investment talks. Ultimately, Iraq's oil ministry convinced him to stay and seek a higher production quota.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Indiana court reverses stepfather's adoption of girl, says mother restricted biological father's access
item.description: An Indiana stepfather’s adoption of his wife’s daughter has been reversed by an appeals court. The ruling found that the biological father's limited contact was largely a result of the mother's attempts to limit his access. Evidence indicated he sought involvement and provided financial support. The majority opinion pointed out discrepancies in the mother’s testimony compared to previous court decisions, leading to a remand for further custody deliberations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Archaeologists digging in Alexandria's ancient royal quarter uncovered massive limestone
item.description: Archaeologists have unveiled an impressive limestone foundation in Alexandria that may belong to a royal tomb. The site, located in the ancient Royal Quarter, features a mysterious tunnel and a distinctive square structure. Experts believe this could be linked to Ptolemy IV Philopator and potentially serve a funerary purpose. A dedicated committee is examining the architectural details, while further excavations promise to illuminate Alexandria's fascinating historical narrative.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Supreme Court orders fresh review of Montana widow's inheritance dispute
item.description: Montana's Supreme Court has mandated that a lower court revisit the distribution of a deceased man's estate to his widow. This legal dispute arose following the death of Jack Raymond Stone, leading his wife Sara Benchoff Stone to file a claim. After Sara's passing, her son continued her pursuit, focusing on the property's valuation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 2,200 shipping containers from Arizona border wall may become affordable rental homes in Tucson
item.description: Boxes of Hope has joined forces with La Frontera to transform steel shipping containers into affordable housing solutions. With a vision to establish between 350 and 450 rental units, the initiative will also provide essential services like behavioral healthcare and job training. Currently in the planning phase, with fundraising underway, the project aims to commence site development by 2027, addressing Tucson's growing affordable housing crisis as many await support.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Wisconsin court rejects prenup after husband's monthly income surpasses $81,000
item.description: In Wisconsin, a marriage contract ignited a lengthy divorce dispute marked by staggering wealth disparities. After almost two decades, Tracy Marie Chernick managed to contest the fairness of their initial agreement. The Wisconsin Court of Appeals determined that Ryan David Chernick had withheld crucial financial details prior to their wedding.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
